units.source_excerpt: Using up to six guesses, players are asked to predict a five-letter word in Wordle, which provides feedback after each guess.
units.reusable_pattern: game-rule summary as abstract opener establishing domain context
reusable_elements: [Game] requires players to [action] within [constraint], which provides [feedback]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not generalize Wordle-specific rules to other word games without adaptation

units.source_excerpt: We all know that different words have various characteristics that could influence how well a player performs. In this regard, our team modeled and evaluated the provided data to arrive at some intriguing conclusions.
units.reusable_pattern: We all know [common knowledge] + In this regard our team [action] to arrive at [outcome] informal scope declaration
reusable_elements: We all know that [domain phenomenon]. In this regard, our team [modeled/analyzed] [data] to arrive at [conclusions]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'we all know' in formal academic writing

units.source_excerpt: For task 1, after data preprocessing, we first use the ARIMA model to forecast the number of reported results and find that it can only capture the linear part.
units.reusable_pattern: For task [N], after [preprocessing], we first use [model] and find that it can only capture [limitation]
reusable_elements: For task [N], after [preprocessing], we first use [Model A] to [goal] and find that it can only capture [part]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use 'first use' without following up with improvement

units.source_excerpt: Second, we take the LSTM model to capture the information of the non-linear part. Finally, we combine them to form ARIMA-LSTM model, which yields more accurate predictions with an RMSE of 0.0432.
units.reusable_pattern: Second we take [model-B] to capture [complement]. Finally we combine to form [hybrid] with [metric]
reusable_elements: Second, we take [Model B] to capture [complement]. Finally, we combine them to form [Hybrid], which yields [metric] of [value]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'take the model' — prefer 'employ' or 'apply'

units.source_excerpt: We finally arrive at a prediction interval of [9614,43109] for March 1, 2023.
units.reusable_pattern: We finally arrive at a prediction interval of [range] for [target-date]
reusable_elements: We finally arrive at a prediction interval of [range] for [date]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report wide intervals without commenting on uncertainty

units.source_excerpt: Subsequently, we define five word attributes, such as syllable count and entropy, and analyze their correlation with the percentage of people reporting scores in the difficult mode through the Spearman correlation coefficient, and find them to be significantly correlated.
units.reusable_pattern: Subsequently we define [N] word attributes and analyze correlation through [technique] and find [result]
reusable_elements: Subsequently, we define [N] [attributes] such as [examples], and analyze their correlation with [DV] through [technique], and find them to be [result]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid triple 'and' coordination in single sentence

units.source_excerpt: For task 2, we use five preferred word attributes and competition number to predict the distribution of results using a stacking model that combines linear regression models (Ridge regression, Lasso regression) and tree models (XGBoost, LightGBM).
units.reusable_pattern: For task [N], we use [inputs] to predict [output] using stacking that combines [type-A] and [type-B]
reusable_elements: For task [N], we use [inputs] to predict [output] using a [ensemble] that combines [models-A] and [models-B]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list model names parenthetically without explaining selection criteria

units.source_excerpt: We find that the stacking model improves the goodness of fit of the prediction results to 83.77%.
units.reusable_pattern: We find that [model] improves [metric] to [value]%
reusable_elements: We find that [model] improves [metric] to [X]%
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report R-squared as percentage without noting it is R-squared

units.source_excerpt: Moreover, the MSE, RMSE, and MAE all indicate that the stacking model has a better capacity for learning.
units.reusable_pattern: Moreover, [metric-A], [metric-B], and [metric-C] all indicate that [model] has [quality]
reusable_elements: Moreover, [metric-A], [metric-B], and [metric-C] all indicate that [model] has [quality]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim 'better capacity' without specifying baseline

units.source_excerpt: On March 1, 2023, the anticipated distribution of 'EERIE' will be [1,2,3,4,5,6,X]=[0,0,9,18,26,37,10].
units.reusable_pattern: On [date], the anticipated distribution of [word] will be [vector]
reusable_elements: On [date], the anticipated distribution of [subject] will be [category-list]=[value-list]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report distributions as raw vectors without explaining categories

units.source_excerpt: For task 3, we select seven additional word attributes to measure the words' difficulty level, and then downscale the metrics by principal component analysis (PCA).
units.reusable_pattern: For task [N], we select [N] additional attributes to measure [target], then downscale by [technique]
reusable_elements: For task [N], we select [N] additional [attributes] to measure [target], and then [reduce] by [technique]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'downscale' for dimensionality reduction

units.source_excerpt: We then use Gaussian Mixture Model(GMM) to cluster the words into three categories: difficult, moderate and easy.
units.reusable_pattern: We then use [Model] to cluster [subjects] into [N] categories: [list]
reusable_elements: We then use [Model] to cluster [subjects] into [N] categories: [category-list]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present clustering categories as ground truth without validation

units.source_excerpt: It demonstrates that our model has a 67% accuracy rate.
units.reusable_pattern: It demonstrates that our model has a [X]% accuracy rate
reusable_elements: It demonstrates that our model has a [X]% accuracy rate
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use 'demonstrates' for modest accuracy

units.source_excerpt: Finally, we classified 'EERIE' into the category of 'difficult' based on its attribute.
units.reusable_pattern: Finally, we classified [example] into category of [label] based on its [basis]
reusable_elements: Finally, we classified [subject] into the category of [label] based on its [attribute/basis]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'category of' — use 'as' for brevity

units.source_excerpt: For task 4, we perform a visual analysis of the provided dataset and discover some intriguing properties in three areas.
units.reusable_pattern: For task [N], we perform visual analysis and discover [qualifier] properties in [N] areas
reusable_elements: For task [N], we perform a visual analysis of [data] and discover [qualifier] properties in [N] areas

units.source_excerpt: We also conduct sensitivity analysis, which shows how different samples affect the word difficulty clustering model.
units.reusable_pattern: We also conduct sensitivity analysis, which shows how [variation] affects [model]
reusable_elements: We also conduct sensitivity analysis, which shows how [variation] affects [model]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not relegate sensitivity analysis to single sentence in abstract

reusable_elements: Keywords: [Model]; [Technique]; [Domain];

units.source_excerpt: Wordle is a daily puzzle offered by The New York Times that requires players to guess a five-letter real word within six attempts to solve, and is now available in more than 60 languages.
units.reusable_pattern: [Subject] is a [category] offered by [entity] that requires [action] within [constraint], available in [scope]
reusable_elements: [Subject] is a [category] offered by [entity] that requires [action] within [constraint], and is now available in [scope]

units.source_excerpt: As Wordle grew in popularity, The New York Times wanted us to analyze and model the data it provided.

reusable_elements: As [subject] grew in [quality], [stakeholder] wanted us to [action] the data it provided

units.source_excerpt: To address these issues, our team will take the following steps.
units.reusable_pattern: To address these issues, our team will take the following steps

units.source_excerpt: An ARIMA-LSTM model was built to predict the number of reported results.
units.reusable_pattern: [Model] was built to [goal] passive task-statement in bullet list

units.source_excerpt: To simplify our problem, we make the following basic assumptions, each of which is sufficiently reasonable.

units.source_excerpt: Assume that on January 1, 2023, March 1, 2023, there are no unexpected factors that will change the data substantially.

units.source_excerpt: Table 1: Notations with Symbols and Description columns

units.source_excerpt: Since we can only use the official COMAP dataset, and the given data is obtained by mining Twitter, there is a possibility of data anomalies, so we pre-processed this part of the data before building the model.
units.reusable_pattern: Since we can only use [dataset], and [source-limitation], there is possibility of [issue], so we [action]
reusable_elements: Since we can only use [official dataset], and [limitation], there is a possibility of [issue], so we [preprocessed]

units.source_excerpt: Fill: We replace the outliers with the average of the before and after data. Reject: We remove the entire data where the sum deviates from 100%.
units.reusable_pattern: Fill: [action for outliers]. Reject: [action for constraint violations]
reusable_elements: Fill: We [action] outliers with [replacement]. Reject: We remove [condition]

units.source_excerpt: Since the data are time series and the amount of data is small, after considering various prediction models, we first chose the ARIMA model.

reusable_elements: Since the data are [type] and [constraint], after considering various [models], we first chose [Model]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'amount of data is small' — specify sample size

units.source_excerpt: In the ARIMA (p, d, q) model, AR is the autoregressive, p is the autoregressive term; MA is the moving average, q is the number of moving average terms, and d is the number of differences.
units.reusable_pattern: In [Model](p,d,q), [component-A] is [def]; [component-B] is [def] parametric definition
reusable_elements: In the [Model]([parameters]), [component] is [definition]; [component] is [definition]

units.source_excerpt: First of all, we perform a smoothness test on the time series rt of Number of reported results.

reusable_elements: First of all, we perform [test] on the [data] of [variable]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'First of all' — use 'First'

units.source_excerpt: The prediction results of the ARIMA model are not very volatile due to the fact that the residual part is not well predicted, so this paper further improves the prediction model by combining ARIMA with LSTM neural network.
units.reusable_pattern: [Model-A] results are [limitation] due to [reason], so this paper further improves by combining [A] with [B]
reusable_elements: [Model-A] results are [limitation] due to [reason], so this paper further improves by combining [A] with [B]

units.source_excerpt: In this section, the ARIMA model was used to predict the number of reported outcomes, and the LSTM model was used to predict the residual series to correct the shortcomings of the ARIMA model.
units.reusable_pattern: In this section, [Model-A] was used to [task-A], and [Model-B] was used to [task-B] to correct [limitation]
reusable_elements: In this section, [Model-A] was used to [task], and [Model-B] was used to [complementary-task] to correct [shortcoming]

units.source_excerpt: To explore whether any attributes of words affect the percentage of people reporting scores in the difficult mode, we first looked for attributes of a number of representative words.

reusable_elements: To explore whether [factors] affect [DV], we first looked for [relevant features]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use 'looked for' — prefer 'identified' or 'examined'

units.source_excerpt: We applied the method of correlation analysis to the five word attribute indicators and the percentage of scores reported in Hard Mode, as measured by the spearman rank correlation coefficient.
units.reusable_pattern: We applied [method] to [inputs] as measured by [technique]
reusable_elements: We applied [method] to [N] [indicators] and [DV], as measured by [technique]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'constructed above' — use section references

units.source_excerpt: As can be seen from the figure6, most of the indicators do not correlate significantly with the proportion of players who choose the difficult mode, and only the number of vowels has a strong positive correlation.
units.reusable_pattern: As can be seen from [figure], most [indicators] do not correlate significantly, only [variable] has [correlation]
reusable_elements: As can be seen from [figure], most [indicators] do not correlate significantly with [DV], and only [variable] has a strong [direction] correlation
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'As can be seen' — state observation directly

units.source_excerpt: In order to predict the distribution of reported results at a given future date and future word, we train seven stacking models to predict the specific proportion of each number of attempts separately.
units.reusable_pattern: In order to predict [target] at [conditions], we train [N] [models] to predict [component] separately
reusable_elements: In order to predict [target] at [conditions], we train [N] [models] to predict [components] separately
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'In order to' — use 'To'

units.source_excerpt: The prediction results show that the linear model is more accurate in predicting data around the mean, while the tree model is more accurate in predicting the distribution of extreme values, and the Stacking fusion model retains the advantages of both models.
units.reusable_pattern: [Results] show [model-A] better at [regime-A], while [model-B] better at [regime-B], and [hybrid] retains advantages of both
reusable_elements: [Results] show that [model-A] is more accurate in [regime-A], while [model-B] is more accurate in [regime-B], and [hybrid] retains the advantages of both

units.source_excerpt: To solve the third problem, we first selected seven English word attributes and features to measure the difficulty level of the words.
units.reusable_pattern: To solve the [ordinal] problem, we first selected [N] [attributes] to measure [target]
reusable_elements: To solve the [ordinal] problem, we first selected [N] [features] to measure [concept]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'solve the problem' — specify what solving means

units.source_excerpt: In order to classify solution words, we built a word classification model based on Gaussian mixture model (GMM).
units.reusable_pattern: In order to [goal], we built a [model-type] based on [technique]
reusable_elements: In order to [classify/predict] [subject], we built a [model] based on [technique]

units.source_excerpt: A Gaussian mixture model is a weighted combination of a series of Gaussian distributions. A Gaussian mixture density function consisting of M components is a linear weighted sum of M density functions.
units.reusable_pattern: [Model] is a weighted combination of [components]. Density function of M components is linear weighted sum
reusable_elements: [Model] is a [weighted combination] of [components]. [Function] consisting of [M] components is a [mathematical-form]

units.source_excerpt: To further classify the data, we used GMM to cluster the words. We called the Python scikit-learn package for GMM to train all the data.
units.reusable_pattern: To further [action], we used [model]. We called Python [package] for [model] to train
reusable_elements: To further [action], we used [model]. We called [language] [package] for [model] to [train/evaluate]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name software packages unless reproducibility requires it

units.source_excerpt: To explore the clustering effect in more detail, we defined the difficulty of each word based on the expected number of guesses and compared it with the classification results.

reusable_elements: To explore [effect], we defined [ground truth] based on [metric] and compared it with [model results]

units.source_excerpt: To test the reasonableness and generalizability of our GMM classification model, we expand the training samples to observe the changes in classification accuracy.
